touches.text: Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).

What the waker starts outlives whoever started it (detached, or through systemd-run --user, which gives it its own memory cap and log while still deciding nothing). Restarting a shim never takes down the bus it once woke. [Q#92: A proof that starts Windows processes stays red until it has your word (CAIRN_PROOF_MAY_SPAWN=1). Measured 2026-11-12: tooth 2 of dc945eb1f072 (cairn.cmd against Git Bash) is red on exactly that word, and nothing in this outline says what the word is. Is it an env var each run sets, a standing flag in ~/.cairn, or may a proof spawn one short hidden process without asking?]
